name: Question 3
problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1-5t \\ y=2+t \\ z=t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1-5t \\ 2+t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-5t \\ t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: {x=1−5ty=2+tz=t What would be the vector equation of the line?

a
 r=[−511]+t[120],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
 None of the listed

 r=t[−511],t∈(−∞,∞)

r=[120]+t[−511],t∈(−∞,∞)
